description: Sets the person's event badge: what they are at the event for, who they want to meet, and whether other attendees there can find them. Needs a personal connector token (a shared token reads but changes nothing), `discoverable` as true or false, and the badge sentences in the person's own words: `headline` (what they are here for) and `lookingFor` (who they want to meet). A badge is findable with both sentences and a first name; a call that would leave one of them blank is refused, and the reply's `needs` lists what is missing. `intent` is optional and takes Buyer, Vendor, Networker or Social; without it the server derives the category from the sentences and falls back to Networker, as the badge in the app does. `label` keeps the person's own word for their category (for example Investor) as written. `firstName` sets the name on the badge; without it the stored name stays as it is. The event is `eventIdOrSlug` or `eventId` when one is given; otherwise it is the one current event the person has joined, and when they have joined none or several the reply says so (with `nextTool` event_redeem_code, or the list of `events`) and nothing changes. It works in two steps: a call without `confirm` returns the sentence describing the change for the person to approve, plus a `confirmToken`, and changes nothing; a call with confirm true and that token writes. The token lasts two minutes, works once, and stops working if any argument changes. A write that carries new words returns `readBack.sentence`, which lists what the matcher scores from them; `facets` ({confirm: true}, {add: [...]} or {remove: [...]}) applies the person's answer to it through the same two steps. It changes only that person's badge at one event.

confirm.description: Absent on the first call, which changes nothing. true, together with confirmToken, makes the change.

confirmToken.description: The token the first call returned. Needed when confirm is true.

discoverable.description: true lists the person where other attendees at that event can find them; false keeps them off that list. It is a separate answer from the intent and is not inferred from it; a missing or non-boolean value is refused rather than defaulted.

eventId.description: Optional. An event id the person has joined. When this and eventIdOrSlug are both absent, the event is the one current event the person has joined.

eventIdOrSlug.description: OPTIONAL. Event id (tie_la_demo), public slug, or the event name, as the events tools accept it. When this and eventId are both absent, the event is the one current event the person has joined.

facets.description: Optional. The person's answer to the read-back: {confirm: true}, {add: [their words]} or {remove: [their words]}. The server maps the words onto the read-back's own list.

firstName.description: Optional. The first name the badge shows, 2 to 40 characters of letters, spaces, hyphens and apostrophes. A badge without a name is not findable. When absent, the stored name is kept; a name the badge cannot take refuses the whole call and the reply says why.

headline.description: What the person is here for, in their own words, up to 280 characters. The first of the two badge sentences: the matcher reads it and other attendees see it, so a full sentence ("raising a seed round for a logistics startup") matches better than a word. Phone numbers, email addresses and links are removed on the server. When absent, the stored sentence is kept.

intent.description: Optional. One of Buyer, Vendor, Networker or Social, as the person said it; case and surrounding spaces are ignored. When absent, the server derives the category from the two sentences and falls back to Networker. A word outside the four belongs in `label`.

intentText.description: Optional. The older name for `lookingFor`; it writes the same badge sentence, up to 280 characters. When both are sent, `lookingFor` is used. Phone numbers, email addresses and links are removed on the server. An absent or empty value leaves the stored sentence as it is.

label.description: Optional. The person's own word for their category when none of the four fits ("Investor", "Director", "Press"). Up to 24 characters of letters, spaces and hyphens. It is kept and shown as written; the server still files one of the four behind it.

lookingFor.description: Who the person wants to meet, in their own words, up to 280 characters. The second badge sentence, the same field the older `intentText` writes. Phone numbers, email addresses and links are removed on the server. When absent, the stored sentence is kept.

requestId.description: An id for this change chosen by the caller, at least 8 characters. A repeat with the same id and the same arguments returns the first result without changing anything a second time.
